title: Deep-learning image search helps identify three Nasca geoglyphs verified in field surveys
summary: A learned object detector trained on pictorial elements from 21 known geoglyphs guided human inspection of aerial-image candidates and subsequent on-site surveys. The 2023 primary report documents verified legs, fish and bird figures. These objects were already among the geoglyphs identified by 2022; this record dates the detailed 2023 report and does not claim they were first discovered that year. A fourth humanoid figure announced in 2019 is excluded from this record.
ai_technology: Deep-learning object detection on multiscale aerial imagery

evidence.tested: Primary university Methods/results describe 307 element/multiscale training images from 21 known figures, human review of model detections and on-site verification of the legs, fish and bird geoglyphs.
evidence.unknown: The documented June 1,2023 report first publishes these three figures’ photographs and illustrations, but says they were already included among 358 geoglyphs identified by 2022. No absolute first-public-discovery priority is claimed. The source-reported 21-fold candidate-search speed comparison is not an independently replicated overall archaeological productivity gain. The earlier 2019 humanoid and separate 2024 catalog result of 303 geoglyphs are not counted here.
evidence.ai_role: A trained deep-learning detector learns pictorial components at multiple image scales and proposes aerial-image candidates for human review and field investigation, directly linking learned image search to the three recorded archaeological finds.

source_review.scope: Exact publisher title/DOI/abstract and full primary university two-page research Methods/results release. Original publisher full paper inaccessible; a third-party journal reproduction was only corroborative and is not treated as authenticated primary Methods.
